# What the data-dict export loses: Medical Expenditure Panel Survey, Household Component (MEPS-HC)

The YAML files here follow data-dict spec 0.1.0. They describe the common data format, so they validate against its parquet files. The records in `metadata/` remain canonical. This table counts what the export drops or flattens into text.

| | `2022` | `2023` | `2024` |
|---|---|---|---|
| variables exported | 83 | 82 | 82 |
| variables whose numeric code labels went to `details` (no labeled numeric codes) | 59 | 59 | 59 |
| missing or unresolved codes, typed only in the `__code` column's labels | 78 | 76 | 75 |
| variables listed by name only (no type the records can support) | 17 | 17 | 17 |
| quantities exported with open range bounds (no valid range recorded) | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| availability entries (wave by form, with n), summarized as one line of text | 83 | 82 | 82 |
| field origins (publisher, data file, rule, hand, model) not exported | 286 | 283 | 283 |
| links between releases, not exported | 164 | 164 | 164 |
| derived properties (scale signatures), not exported | 30 | 30 | 30 |
| release id not expressible as data-dict `version` (needs semver or a date) | 1 | 1 | 1 |
